newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher on export hopes, Sparks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher on export hopes, Sparks.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on optimism for sales this week of U.S. wheat to several countries with talk a wheat acreage estimate was released by a Sparks Companies official also mentioned, traders said.
"There's some wheat business around," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co, referring to trade hopes for a sale of U.S. wheat to Turkey, Algeria and Pakistan.
Traders said there was talk that analytical firm Sparks Companies had cut by two million acres its outlook for 1997 U.S. winter wheat.
But Sparks CEO Carrol Brunthaver also said Monday at a conference in Kansas City that CBOT July wheat would trade below $3.00 per bushel during harvest next summer.
Support to the market also came from the posting Tuesday of no deliveries on the December contract and perceptions that recent stopping of the deliveries was done by U.S. mills.
"There were no deliveries and good stoppers when there have been deliveries," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Wheat closed five cents per bushel higher to 1-1/4 lower, with December up 3-1/2 at $3.93-1/2 a bushel.
Key players included Refco Inc with three million bushels purchased in the March and SAK Futures also bought three million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, above the 7,962 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc sold 100 March $3.50 puts at 4-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 2,500 contracts, above the 1,465 traded Monday.
